pageCache.text:
Welcome to Focus 1st Academy
Specialising in Social, Emotional and Mental Health
A message from our Executive Headteacher
Discover our schools
OUR PROMISE
WE CARE
Our team nurtures each individual in a friendly and hospitable learning environment allowing each student to reach their potential.
QUALITY EDUCATION
Our aim here at Focus 1st Academy is to provide high quality education and training delivered with recognised qualification.
WE BELIEVE
We believe that all individuals have a certain quality, which is sometimes concealed due to lack of confidence, mixed sentiments or disabilities.
SAFETY MEASURES IN PLACE
We do everything to ensure the health, safety and well-being of our students and employees.
SHOP SCHOOL UNIFORM
3 in 1 Classic Jacket
Rucksack with front pocket
Straight Leg Joggers

At Focus 1st Academy, we believe every young person deserves an education that understands them, supports them, and helps them flourish. As a specialist alternative provision school focusing on Social, Emotional and Mental Health (SEMH), we provide a nurturing, personalised environment where students are known, valued and empowered.Our dedicated team is committed to unlocking potential and building confidence. We deliver high-quality education with recognised qualifications, ensuring our young people are equipped not just for exams, but for life. We believe that every individual carries a unique spark — sometimes that spark is hard to see, but with the right support, it shines.Underpinned by a culture of care, respect and safety, we maintain rigorous standards of wellbeing and safeguarding so students can thrive without barriers. Our promise is simple: we care; we deliver excellence; we believe in every student.If you’re looking for a school where relationships, tailored learning and growth matter first, Focus 1st Academy is where your journey begins.
MEET OUR HEADTEACHERS
Executive Headteacher
As the founder of Focus 1st Academy 25 years ago, my mission has always come from a deeply personal place — to build a school where every child feels seen, valued, heard and safe. A place where inclusion isn’t just a principle, but a practice woven into every corner of school life. I’ve worked tirelessly to create an environment that embraces all pupils, including those facing visible disabilities, hidden needs, or personal challenges with mixed sentiments that too often go unnoticed. Every child deserves the chance to thrive, to feel they truly belong. For our hands-on learners, we prioritise practical, meaningful experiences — not just to meet academic goals, but to build confidence, real-life skills, and the foundation to become respectful, law-abiding citizens who can participate fully and proudly in society. My commitment remains the same today as it was at the beginning: to make sure every child, no matter their starting point, matters and is equipped with the tools they need to succeed.
We deliver various vocational programmes, GCSEs Math’s, English, Science, ICT and Functional skills in Math’s and English. Our students at Arnos Grove are time tabled to enjoy a variety of sport activities off site weekly. Our Cheshunt and Welwyn pupils benefit from all the on-site facilities which are implemented into our curriculum, these include football, basketball, squash, swimming, dance, badminton and much more.
Focus 1st has developed an approach to learning that acts as a vehicle to motivate and improve individuals’ prospects. Whilst all individuals are encouraged towards gaining recognised qualifications, we also believe that the process of skill enhancement, confidence and self-esteem building is as vital as the outcome.
We cater to pupils aged 11-16 year who are identified by schools/local authorities as more able to fulfil their potential by pursuing education outside the school environment, risk of PEX, SEMH, non attendees, require additional support, SEN or are out of education. The aim to equip students with the appropriate skills, experience and qualifications to participate in modern society at post 16.
We strive to support the well-being and mental health of each individual, encourage self-worth and confidence building, through small interventions. Lessons are shaped to support their academic learning as well as incorporate an abundance of physical and practical activities. Our experienced and nurturing staff take a more creative approach to their teaching style which provides an outlet and a platform for self-expression and exploration.
ETHOS​
Our hands-on approach to learning creates an inspirational motivation for our students and are taught methods on how to improve their social skills in preparation for work/apprenticeship schemes and/or further education by learning in real-life situations. We believe that all individuals have a certain quality, which is sometimes concealed due to lack of confidence, mixed sentiments or disabilities. As such, recognising and coming to terms with barriers is a small part of the conflict, we are certain that all individuals are aware of their own weaknesses; the most vital part is engaging with professionals and adhere to individual training plans set which in turn prepares our students for economic and social integration into adulthood.
BRITISH VALUES
The British values are a set of principles that underpin the way of life in the United Kingdom.
These values are as follows:
Acceptance for those with different faiths and beliefs
We at Focus 1st Academy explicitly teach British values through specific lessons or activities that promote democracy, the rule of law, individual liberty, mutual respect and tolerance of different faiths and beliefs. We foster a positive school culture that promotes British values by celebrating diversity, encouraging respectful behaviour, and promoting a sense of community and belonging. We encourage student participation in school decision-making processes, such as through school councils, to promote democracy and give students a voice. We promote critical thinking skills by encouraging students to question and challenge ideas, and consider different perspectives and viewpoints. We offer opportunities for students to learn about different cultures and religions, and to interact with people from diverse backgrounds, to promote mutual respect and tolerance.

SAFEGAURDING & ONLINE SAFETY
At Focus 1st Academy, the safety and wellbeing of our pupils is our top priority. We are committed to providing a caring, supportive environment where every young person feels safe, respected, and able to reach their full potential. Safeguarding is central to everything we do, and we work closely with pupils, families, and external agencies to ensure all members of our school community are protected from harm.
In an increasingly digital world, online safety is a vital part of our safeguarding approach. We help pupils develop the knowledge and skills to use technology safely, respectfully, and responsibly. Through our curriculum and ongoing guidance, we empower them to recognise potential risks online and to know what to do if they ever feel unsafe or unsure.
All staff at Focus 1st Academy receive regular safeguarding and online safety training to ensure they can identify concerns early and provide effective support. On this page, you’ll also find a range of helpful resources, guidance, and links to support parents, carers, and pupils in staying safe both in school and online.
If you have any concerns about the safety or wellbeing of a pupil, please contact our Designated Safeguarding Lead (DSL) or a member of our safeguarding team.

FOR PARENTS/ CARERS
Welcome to the Focus 1st Academy Parent Portal — your hub for information, guidance, and support to help you and your child make the most of their learning journey. At Focus 1st Academy, we believe that strong partnerships between school and home are key to every pupil’s success. This page brings together a range of useful resources, advice, and links designed to help parents and carers support their child’s education, wellbeing, and personal development. Here, you’ll find practical information and guidance on topics such as behaviour and expectations, learning difficulties and additional support needs, and mental health and emotional wellbeing. Whether you’re looking for strategies to support learning at home, advice on accessing specialist help, or tips on promoting positive routines and resilience, this page is here to help. If you would like further information or support, please contact your child’s Tutor, or a member of our Pastoral Team. We are always here to work with you in supporting your child’s progress and wellbeing.

SAFEGAURDING TEAM
At Focus 1st Academy, safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children is our highest priority. In line with Keeping Children Safe in Education and Working Together to Safeguard Children, we ensure all staff are trained, vigilant and confident in recognising, recording and reporting concerns. We follow clear procedures, work closely with external agencies, and maintain a culture where safeguarding is everyone’s responsibility. Our shared commitment ensures every young person is safe, supported and able to thrive.

EXECUTIVE HEADTEACHER
As the founder of Focus 1st Academy 25 years ago, my mission has always come from a deeply personal place — to build a school where every child feels seen, valued, heard and safe. A place where inclusion isn’t just a principle, but a practice woven into every corner of school life.
I’ve worked tirelessly to create an environment that embraces all pupils, including those facing visible disabilities, hidden needs, or personal challenges with mixed sentiments that too often go unnoticed. Every child deserves the chance to thrive, to feel they truly belong.
For our hands-on learners, we prioritise practical, meaningful experiences — not just to meet academic goals, but to build confidence, real-life skills, and the foundation to become respectful, law-abiding citizens who can participate fully and proudly in society. My commitment remains the same today as it was at the beginning: to make sure every child, no matter their starting point, matters and is equipped with the tools they need to succeed.
ANDREA KATTIRTZI
HEADTEACHER (Cheshunt & Welwyn)
At our Cheshunt and Welwyn campuses, the well-being and mental health of our pupils are at the heart of everything we do. We believe that a supportive, nurturing environment is the foundation for learning and personal growth.
As sports-driven schools, we encourage our students to stay active and engaged through a variety of daily activities including swimming, badminton, table tennis, and more. These not only promote physical health but also help build confidence, teamwork, and resilience.
Academically, we offer a broad and balanced curriculum. Pupils have the opportunity to achieve GCSEs in core subjects such as Maths, English, Science, Art, and Textiles. We are equally proud of our strong vocational pathways, which include courses in Beauty, Hairdressing, Barbering, and Cookery – helping students gain real-world skills for future careers.
Our goal is to provide a vibrant, inclusive learning environment where every pupil can thrive, both academically and personally.

pageCache.text:
STUDENT HEALTH & WELLBEING
At Focus 1st Academy, we believe that happy, healthy pupils learn best. We are committed to supporting the physical, emotional, and mental wellbeing of every young person in our care. Our aim is to create an inclusive and nurturing environment where pupils feel confident, valued, and supported to reach their full potential.
We take a proactive approach to wellbeing, promoting positive mental health through our curriculum, enrichment activities, and everyday school culture. Pupils are encouraged to talk openly about how they feel and to seek help whenever they need it. Our dedicated staff are always here to listen and provide guidance, and we work closely with families and external professionals to ensure that every pupil receives the right support.
On this page, you’ll find a range of useful resources, advice, and links to help pupils, parents, and carers look after health and wellbeing both inside and outside of school. If you have any concerns about a pupil’s health or wellbeing, please contact a member of our Wellbeing Team or speak with your child’s Tutor.
